clue.text: Greatly inspiring northern artist

indicators.note: inspiring is read literally as breathing in, so the first word takes the second one inside it

parts.note: greatly means much, as in 'much improved'

explanation.surface: Praise for a painter from the north whose work moves people deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like praise for the painter, but it means taking in: MUCH breathes in N.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Munch was the Norwegian painter of The Scream, so he is a particular example of an artist.

clue.text: Criminal dominates Kent town

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongdoing, so the letters are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crime boss holds sway over a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, and this is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is the county town of Kent in south-east England.

clue.text: Chip from Ohio is able to head north

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OH is the US postal abbreviation for Ohio
can means is able

explanation.surface: A snack from Ohio can travel north.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served with cheese or salsa.

clue.text: Dissident at this time attracting limitless criticism

indicators.note: attracting means drawing something to oneself, so the second piece joins the first

parts.note: here can mean now, at this point

indicators.note: limitless means without its limits, so both end letters are dropped

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in 'took some stick'

explanation.surface: A rebel is currently attracting unrelenting criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limitless' reads as 'endless' criticism, but means trimming both ends off STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views at odds with accepted doctrine, so is a dissenter.

clue.text: Defend crazy fears a drug has run out

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of the words that follow have gone wild and are rearranged
has run out says one of the letters named must be removed from the jumbled pool

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A drug runs out and someone panicking tries to protect themselves from irrational worries.
explanation.walkthrough: FEARS A DRUG has one R too many; taking out R (run) leaves the letters to rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To safeguard something is to protect it from harm, the same as defending it.

clue.text: Detestable group that may interrupt cricket match?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a contemptible bunch of people
second meaning: a brief fall of rain that stops play

explanation.walkthrough: Calling a group 'a shower' is British slang for a useless lot; rain regularly halts cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Shower means both a brief spell of rain, which halts cricket, and in British slang a contemptible bunch of people.

clue.text: Concern about mum meeting footballers in place of young swimmers

indicators.note: about says the business word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a concern is a business, a firm
mum as in 'keep mum' means hush, SH
FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body

explanation.surface: A business worried about a mother meeting a football team at a children's swimming venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother but the instruction to be silent, SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm rears fish in tanks or pens, so it is a place where young fish are raised.

clue.text: Scowl from stern expert

parts.note: grim means stern or forbidding
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A severe specialist gives a dark look.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of disgust or pain, much like a frowning look.

clue.text: Impressive golfing feat, something Jack will never shoot?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hole completed three strokes under par
second meaning: Jack is a sailor, and sailors dread killing this seabird after The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.walkthrough: Jack (Jack Tar) is a sailor, not golfer Jack Nicklaus, and in Coleridge's poem shooting the bird brings disaster on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the word names a score of three under par; it is also the great seabird sailors consider unlucky to kill.

clue.text: Gloomy medic touring department, heading off

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the medic's letters surround the rest

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: an area can mean a field or department of activity

explanation.surface: A doctor walking round a hospital department looks miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dull and depressing.

clue.text: Sustain debts without any interest

parts.note: to sustain a loss or cost is to incur it
IOUs are written acknowledgments of debts

explanation.surface: Someone running up debts without paying any interest on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' in the surface is financial; in the definition it means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: An incurious person shows no curiosity, so has no interest in finding things out.

clue.text: This writer's depresssed, downing large tincture

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves; 'this writer is' contracts to I'M

indicators.note: downing means knocking down, so the abbreviation for large is dropped out of the mood word

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A gloomy writer downs a large measure of medicinal tincture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downing' looks like drinking the tincture, but it means getting rid of the L. 'Tincture' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To tincture something is to tinge or permeate it with a quality, which is exactly what imbue means.

clue.text: Obligation to pursue small bed for dog

indicators.note: to pursue is to come after, so the obligation word follows the other pieces

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a tie is a binding obligation

explanation.surface: A dog owner feels bound to chase after a little bed for the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is a Scottish terrier, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Smoother soap

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more flat, comparative of flat
second meaning: to soft-soap, to praise insincerely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' looks like a noun for something that makes skin smoother, but it is a verb, as in soft-soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatter is the comparative of flat (more level), and also a verb for buttering someone up with excessive praise.

clue.text: Two ways US gangster can make a hit in business

definitions.note: second meaning: a duty or function, one's business

parts.note: the first of two ways an American gangster says kill: to off someone
the second way: to ice someone is also US gangster slang for to kill

explanation.surface: A mobster weighing two methods of carrying out a contract killing as part of his trade.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hit' here is a killing; OFF and ICE are both US slang for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a place of business, or a duty and function, so the word stands for business.

clue.text: A full set's played, getting every first serve in?

indicators.note: played suggests the letters have been put into action in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis player completes a whole set without missing a first serve.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a serve landing out is a fault, so getting every first serve in means no faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Faultless means without error; in tennis a serve that misses is a fault, so serving perfectly is error-free.

clue.text: Vigour she developed after losing husband, it's dreadful

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters have been worked into a new form, so rearrange them
after losing says one named letter leaves the jumbled pool

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A widow found new energy after her husband died, a dreadful time.
explanation.walkthrough: VIGOUR SHE without H (husband) leaves eight letters that rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievous means very severe or serious, as in grievous harm, so it matches dreadful.

clue.text: Mock new article upset Etihad outfit's tackling

indicators.note: tackling means taking on, so the club name grips the other letters inside it
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Manchester City play at the Etihad Stadium, so the outfit is City, with the apostrophe s
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A football team in a fresh kit is unsettled while a piece of paper tackles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Etihad is Manchester City's ground; CITY'S read upwards is SYTIC, which takes in N and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock means imitation or fake, and synthetic means artificial, made to imitate something natural.

clue.text: Corroborate representation of nun with pride

indicators.note: a representation shows something in another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Confirming that a picture shows a proud nun.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin an argument is to support it with evidence, which is what corroborating does.

clue.text: Over the moon living around outskirts of Ullapool

indicators.note: around says the word for living wraps itself about the letters picked

parts.note: extant means still existing or alive

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the first and last letters of the name are used

parts.note: a fishing village in the Scottish Highlands; its outer letters are U and L

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be living just outside a Highland village.
explanation.walkthrough: Ullapool is a small town in north-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being over the moon is an idiom for being delighted, and exultant means jubilant.

clue.text: Bound to require credit, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer is a word pronounced like the one given

parts.note: trust means credit, as in buying on trust

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to need a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'certain to', but 'Bound' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means tied up tightly, as a chicken is before roasting, so it means bound.

clue.text: Cleric is source of petty crime

indicators.note: source of means the beginning, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of petty
arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property

explanation.surface: A vicar is blamed as the cause of minor wrongdoing in the parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty crime' reads as one phrase but splits: the first letter of 'petty', then a specific crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a member of the clergy, especially a parish priest, so he is a cleric.

clue.text: Checks regularly Laura's purchasing holiday

indicators.note: purchasing means taking in or acquiring, so the picked letters hold the break inside them
regularly means taking every other letter of the name

parts.note: every other letter of Laura's, starting with the second, gives A, R, S
a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: Laura often buys a break and keeps an eye on things.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt or stop it, as checks do; both mean restrain.

clue.text: Disclose European vehicle at first has nothing revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary is taken as turning round, so the whole string is read backwards
at first means only the first letter of vehicle is taken

parts.note: first letter of vehicle
love is zero, nothing, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Revealing that a European vehicle is at first nothing radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like an adjective describing the car, but it signals reversal of E + V + LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In an old sense evolve means to unfold or open out, so to reveal or bring to light.

clue.text: Become prominent initially opposing cheeky cut by broadband provider

indicators.note: cut by says the first part is split open and the provider is set into the gap
initially means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of opposing
rude means impertinent or cheeky
BT, British Telecom, is a UK telecoms company selling broadband

explanation.surface: A rude remark about an internet company leads to someone standing out.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is the British telecoms firm, a common crossword source for those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to stick out or push forward noticeably, so it means to stand out conspicuously.

clue.text: Ship that belches out steam, not British

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for British is left out

parts.note: a boiler heats water and gives off steam

explanation.surface: A steamship pouring out smoke that is not British-built.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a tanker vessel carrying oil, often to refuel other ships at sea.

clue.text: Brief infatuation over comedian Kumar in Japan, maybe

indicators.note: over says the shortened word is turned the other way round
brief tells us to cut the final letter from the word

parts.note: a rave can mean an enthusiasm or craze for something
Nish Kumar is a British stand-up comedian

explanation.surface: A comedian's short-lived crush, perhaps while touring Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' is not the country but a black lacquer, and as a verb to coat with it. Nish Kumar is a British comedian and TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a hard glossy lacquer, so it is an example of varnish.

clue.text: Turn of phrase did I omit to employ?

indicators.note: to employ means to have something in use, so the letters are held inside the words given

explanation.surface: A writer worrying whether a particular expression was left out.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression whose meaning cannot be deduced from its words, a turn of phrase.

clue.text: Swaps round hands in dances, producing smirks

indicators.note: the hands are right and left, R and L, and swapping them round exchanges those two letters in the dance word

parts.note: reels are lively Scottish dances

explanation.surface: Dancers change partners mid-reel, and it brings on knowing grins.
explanation.walkthrough: Exchanging R (right) and L (left) in REELS turns it into a word for sly looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Leers are sly or suggestive looks, close to smirks as smug unpleasant expressions.

clue.text: Article of clothing this poor scruffy student wears

indicators.note: wears says the jumbled letters have the learner's letter on them, so it goes inside
scruffy suggests untidiness, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A garment worn by a hard-up, untidy student.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo shirt is a casual short-sleeved collared top, an item of clothing.

clue.text: House belonging to retired Alec Ned is erecting

indicators.note: retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
belonging to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Two men named Alec and Ned building a home after leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a home, the place where someone lives, as is a house.

clue.text: Spice French author recalled

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the author's name runs backwards

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French novelist, author of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A French writer remembers a particular seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a tangy red powder from dried berries used as a seasoning in Middle Eastern cooking.
